spec_match.rationale: Executes three normative writeDatagrams/createWritable rules with the spec text quoted beside each observed outcome: non-BufferSource TypeError, oversized resolve-and-discard, and cross-transport sendGroup TypeError.

interactive.rationale: One button runs all three real calls (timeout-raced so nothing can wedge) and colors each outcome against the spec's requirement.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises exactly these three rules executed; the page adds the why-the-discard-rule-is-a-trap explainer.

edge_cases.rationale: The page IS the edge cases, and it also handles no-surface builds, distinguishes legacy-writable results (labelled), and treats a pre-155 mismatch as documented history rather than a page failure.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus, the writeDatagrams procedure, and the createWritable steps.

conformance.rationale: The suite's two async assertions execute the same rules: non-buffersource-write-rejects-typeerror genuinely PASSES on Chromium 141 via the legacy writable, and oversized-write-resolves-and-discards honestly FAILS there (141 rejects oversized writes — real history the spec's resolve rule replaced).

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via the repo CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): run driven at 1280×900 and 360×740 — rule 1 matched (TypeError via legacy writable), rule 2 recorded the real mismatch (141 rejected the 2048-byte write; the spec requires resolve-and-discard), rule 3 honestly untestable without createSendGroup; overflowX 0, zero failed requests. Partial: the all-match outcome and rule 3 need a 155+/flagged build.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the run with per-rule results; all writes raced against timeouts and all session promises claimed, so nothing leaks as unhandled.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; match/mismatch outcomes border emerald/rose with full text; spec quotes are italic charcoal on stone.

accessibility.rationale: Each rule's outcome is its own polite region, the summary is another, the single control is a native 44px button, and outcomes are text-first.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Driven at both classes with 0px horizontal overflow; outcome lines wrap monospace content; both screenshots read.

openQuestions.title: Confirm all-match on a 155+ build
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome 155+ (or the WebTransportSendGroup+WebTransportDatagramsWritable flags), rule 2 should flip to resolve-and-discard via a createWritable lane and rule 3 should throw the cross-transport TypeError, making the summary read 3/3 matched.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region status readout for async API probe result
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Separate polite regions for separate result surfaces; final text, not interstitials.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each rule's outcome paragraph and the summary are distinct polite regions written once per run; the only interstitial (Running…) is replaced in the same region.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive stacked rule cards without horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Single-column stacked sections with wrapping monospace output.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Rules render as stacked bordered cards; outcome boxes use overflow-wrap:anywhere; 0px page overflow at 360px.

summary: Three normative write rules executed for real with the spec text quoted beside each observed result — including the genuine historical mismatch on Chromium 141, where oversized datagram writes reject instead of the spec's resolve-and-discard. Verified with the repo headless-Chromium CDP harness (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud environment); clean console/network, 0px overflow both classes.
